title: Emrys and the Cover
premise: Gideon Vane, a whistle-blower living under four names, is jolted out of fifteen years of careful invisibility when a dead colleague's voiceprint unlocks a server in Riga containing evidence that Gideon's own testimony was used to build a kill-list. The defector who can corroborate it, Mara Ilic, may be bait dangled by the intelligence service Gideon once trusted. As border checkpoints shift and loyalties fracture, Gideon must choose between erasing the trail forever and burning every alias to expose the truth. In the end, Gideon sacrifices their final identity to get Mara and the server contents across the border, emerging nameless but finally free.
about_author: Felix Lockridge is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent a decade writing security protocols for firms he is contractually barred from naming. He writes thrillers from a coastal town where, he insists, nobody knows his real name either.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A quiet morning in Porto under the name 'Daniel Reeve' is shattered when a dead colleague's voiceprint arrives by courier, addressed to a name Gideon abandoned years ago. The emotional beat is dread: someone is mapping the architecture of Gideon's hidden life, and the rules that kept them safe have just been rewritten.

chapters.title: The Riga Server
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Following the voiceprint's coordinates, Gideon remotely unlocks an encrypted server in Latvia and finds their own fifteen-year-old testimony, repurposed into a targeting dossier. The beat is vertigo—Gideon's act of conscience became a weapon, and someone wanted them to know it.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Weather
chapters.summary: Mara Ilic's POV. A disgraced analyst in Riga, Mara discovers she's being groomed as bait in an operation she can't see the edges of. She copies the dossier and runs. The beat is claustrophobic resolve: she knows the border checkpoints change shifts at dawn, and dawn is coming.

chapters.title: Contact Protocol
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A handler Gideon buried a decade ago makes contact, offering protection in exchange for silence. Gideon pretends to negotiate while planning escape, feeling the old pull of institutional loyalty war with hard-earned paranoia. The beat is a chess game where every piece is compromised.

chapters.title: The Ferry at Ventspils
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Gideon and Mara meet for the first time, each testing whether the other is the trap. A near-miss with surveillance forces them onto a freight ferry together. The beat is wary, reluctant trust—two liars recognizing the same craft in each other.

chapters.title: What the Dossier Says
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Aboard the ferry, Mara decrypts the full dossier and finds Gideon's name listed not as a source but as a future target—kept alive because a living whistle-blower discredits the archive. The beat is horrified compassion: Gideon was never a loose end, they were an exhibit.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Ledger
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon confronts the handler in a safehouse in Gdansk and learns the operation's architect is someone Gideon once loved and protected. The beat is grief weaponized—loyalty finally breaks, and Gideon commits to burning every alias to publish the truth.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The plan to cross at the border checkpoint during shift change goes wrong when the schedule is moved up an hour—their leak inside the service was a plant. Pursuit closes in on both sides of the crossing. The beat is escalating panic as the trap snaps shut.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, climax. Cornered at the checkpoint, Gideon realizes the only way through is to become the bait themselves—broadcasting their location to draw the hunters while Mara crosses with the decrypted archive. The beat is sacrificial clarity: the last identity dies so the truth survives.

chapters.title: No Name at All
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, resolution. Weeks later, the dossier is public, careers have fallen, and Mara publishes the story under both their names. She receives an unsigned postcard from a town Gideon once mentioned—a signal of survival, nothing more. The beat is bittersweet release: Gideon is finally invisible by choice, not fear, and free.
